question.text: Per Table 2.3 in NISM Ch 2.5, which of the following is explicitly listed as a LIMITATION of alternative investments?

answer.text: Guaranteed minimum returns imposed by SEBI
Complex fund structuring, less transparency, illiquidity, and difficulty in satisfying regular-income requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Table 2.3, the listed limitations are: (i) complex fund structures hard for investors to comprehend, (ii) complex contractual terms requiring professional support, (iii) less transparency vs traditional, (iv) more complex return determination methodologies, (v) illiquidity due to long investment cycles, and (vi) do not satisfy regular-income requirements. The Trap: Option A — AIFs don't publish daily NAV; that's a Mutual Fund feature. Options C and D are fabricated regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B distributor tests this as a 'disclose to client' list. XIX-C tests it as LP-pitch honesty — your IM and PPM should openly address these. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pre-empt these limitations in your LP due-diligence questionnaire response. LPs reward managers who raise the illiquidity and complexity objections themselves, with mitigation design (staggered drawdowns, side letters on co-invest rights). LPs who discover these limitations in a post-commitment memo become hostile.
